answer: A Sybil attack can be capped by a bonded sponsor trellis. Each new agent identity must be vouched for by an existing staked agent, and that sponsor's stake is slashed if the newcomer proves fake. Forging many identities thus needs many sponsors each risking real capital, so the attacker's cost rises with every extra account instead of staying flat. Reputation cannot be transferred, and a fresh key restarts at zero facing the same audit spiral: one bad attestation wipes out the whole gale of clones at once. Capturing a real share of the network costs more than it yields.
